thread:
Ian: Quick question — when people create experiments in Console, how should the routing predicate DSL interact with per-variant quotas? e.g. if a predicate filters users and a variant runs out of quota, what's the expected fallback?
Maria: Good callout. UX needs to be explicit. Two quick options: 1) server-side validation that ensures any predicate + quota combo has a guaranteed fallback, or 2) allow creation and surface a runtime "quota exhausted" route that routes to holdback.
David: Leaning to #2. Validating every possible runtime combination is hard (rolling audiences, changing attributes). we should provide strong warnings and a live preview instead.
Alex: Preview is key. If Console can evaluate predicate against sampling of recent users and show expected funnel + quotas it helps. Also need clear telemetry events when variant quota hits X% and when fallback fired.
Sam: Agree on telemetry. Events we need: experiment.assign_attempt, experiment.assigned_variant, experiment.quota_exhausted (with reason code), experiment.fallback_variant. These will feed alerts / regression hooks.
Emily: For fallback semantics: prefer deterministic fallback ordering instead of random. e.g. if variant A exhausted, route to B (if compatible) else to holdback. That makes metrics easier.
Ian: What does "compatible" mean? Different predicates may not apply across variants. We should define compatibility as: variant B's routing predicate evaluates to true for the same user context OR variant B has a global predicate (always-true).
Maria: Might be confusing to users. Suggestion: add a "fallback chain" field on the variant config in the Console UI where user can explicitly list fallback variants and whether to respect predicates on fallback.
David: Implementation note: runtime decision flow would be: 1) evaluate predicates in assignment order, 2) check quota, 3) if exhausted consult fallback chain, 4) if none, use global holdback. That avoids unpredictable cross-variant predicate mismatches.
Alex: Also discuss hashing and traffic split: should we hash user id first, then apply predicate? If we hash first, splits are stable even if predicates change; if predicate first, switching predicates changes reachable population distribution.
Sam: Our current API v2 does hash first then filter, which gives more stable per-variant capacity planning. That behavior should be documented in Console UX and in the SDKs.
Emily: Small example for Console copy: ````
// example predicate DSL
country == "US" && (tier == "paid" || experiment_tag == "on")
````
If we hash user id -> assign variant -> then evaluate predicate, you can end up with assigned but filtered users — leads to wasted quota. Hash-first then filter is only good if you then reassign to another variant when filtered out.
Ian: Right, which ties back to deterministic fallback chain. If we hash-first, fallback must be allowed to pick a different variant post-filter.
Maria: UX concern: when user creates experiment we should show a warning card: "Predicates may reduce effective traffic by ~X% — this affects quota consumption and ramp plans." Include a preview button that shows sampled user IDs and where they'd go, plus a checkbox to enable deterministic fallback chain.
David: On API debate: Should Console call a validation endpoint that simulates assignment across N synthetic users and return coverage metrics? I'd say yes — keep validation lightweight and optional, not blocking create.
Alex: I can add a lightweight simulator to the experiment-creation API that runs N=500 samples across population distribution using telemetry histograms. It returns distribution and a small set of example IDs. That will power the preview UI.
Sam: Add server-side alarms: emit an alert when quota consumption rate deviates > 2x expected during ramp or when fallback rate > 1% for >= 5m. These can hook to the Console timeline and to PagerDuty for critical experiments.
Emily: Edge cases: time-windowed quotas (e.g., 1000 assigns per hour) need an eviction policy. If exhausted mid-hour we should still honor fallback chain and record allocation latency metrics. Also: backfilled users (bulk imports) should have a different cost model.
Ian: Good list. Action items: Alex will prototype the simulator API (ETA 3 days). Maria will mock the preview + fallback-chain UI copy (ETA 2 days). Sam/David will draft telemetry event schema and alert thresholds (ETA 2 days). Emily will write the compatibility and deterministic fallback spec (ETA 4 days). I'll open a CR for the Console copy and link it here.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: feature/experiment-sim -> staging at 2021-09-03T18:20:00Z :rocket:
Maria: One more thing — Console should show a small inline explanation when people toggle per-variant quota: "Quota limits assignment attempts, not successful role executions." and a link to docs.
David: SGTM. If we do the simulator, include an opt-out checkbox to not store sampled IDs (privacy). Keep throughput simulator ephemeral.
Alex: Noted. I'll add an anonymization step.
Sam: I'll model alert burn rates and post a sample PromQL in the doc.
Emily: OK — sounds like a plan. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
